title: Senior Manager, Technology Internal Audit
description: We're transforming the grocery industry At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers. Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table. Instacart is a Flex First team There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work. Senior Manager, Technology Internal Audit Job #TAUD41 Overview Maplebear Inc. D/B/A Instacart in San Francisco, CA seeks Senior Manager, Technology Internal Audit (Multiple Openings). Employee may be stationed anywhere in the continental U.S., but will report to headquarters in San Francisco, CA. About the Job Responsible for identifying, assessing, and monitoring key accounting risks and controls to develop solutions that align with the company’s long-term objectives. Duties include: Conducting comprehensive evaluations of risks and internal controls under financial compliance and other regulatory frameworks to ensure accuracy and efficiency; Advising on improvement areas related to engineering and technology systems and practices to support business growth, including assessing risk and controls related to ERP systems; Developing and implementing risk management strategies by leveraging data analytics, automation tools, and artificial intelligence to streamline audit processes; Overseeing the design and execution of internal audit team strategies to evaluate team metrics and support performance improvements; Collaborating with senior management and audit committees to share audit findings with external auditors; Developing comprehensive reports and dashboards to present high-impact findings and actionable recommendations to leadership teams; Other duties as assigned. About You Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Information Technology, or related discipline (or foreign equivalent). 4 years of experience in the job offered or related. 4 years of experience working with financial reporting systems and related reporting tools; 4 years of experience with accounting and audit standards including GAAP and GAAS; 4 years of experience evaluating risks and designing or assessing controls over internally developed (homegrown) technology platforms and environments; 4 years of experience assessing the design and operating effectiveness of information technology general controls (ITGCs) and automated financial controls; 4 years of experience executing internal audit engagements, including pre-IPO readiness and SOX compliance assessments; 4 years of experience leveraging advanced data analytics and automation tools (such as Alteryx, SQL, Python, or comparable technologies) to support audit and risk activities. Instacart provides highly market-competitive compensation and benefits in each location where our employees work. title: Audit Manager, Credit
description: Application Deadline: 11/29/2026 Address: 320 S Canal Street Job Family Group: Audit, Risk & Compliance Audit Manager, Credit Description: Under the direction of the U.S. Audit Director and Senior Audit Manager, the Audit Manager is accountable to support the Enterprise in maintaining effective management processes and system of internal control through the independent execution of audits covering designated U.S. Banking and North American retail and/or commercial segments and Corporate Support Areas. Audits will broadly evaluate the adequacy of control design and operational effectiveness of designed controls. Specific core activities include: Audit execution: Support the Senior Audit Manager in the audit planning and engagement process. Execute all assigned audit engagement activities timely and in accordance with Audit Methodology. Document clear, concise, complete, and supportable work papers for test procedures executed. Assess and recommend action plans to resolve identified control deficiencies using sound judgement. Support the Senior Audit Manager in analyzing and compiling audit results recommending rating area and overall audit engagement ratings. Credit Assessment: Review assigned loans and provide an independent risk assessment including an evaluation of adherence to credit policies and procedures, effectiveness and accuracy of credit and collateral monitoring, underwriting quality, accuracy of documentation, and identification and management of problem credits as defined within the audit scope. Governance Assessment: Assess the auditable units’ risk governance effectiveness over their credit portfolios and alignment with the Bank’s risk appetite framework. Areas of assessment may include policy effectiveness, risk management and reporting, risk oversight, and strategic management. Regulatory Review: Evaluate compliance with applicable U.S. banking laws, regulations, regulatory guidance, and Bank policies within the audit scope, and assess whether related controls are appropriately designed and operating effectively. Business Operations: Assess key business operations and end-to-end processes to determine whether responsibilities, procedures, systems, and controls support effective credit administration, risk management, and reliable execution. Other Core Activities: Data Analytics: Use high value data analytics, where appropriate, to enhance risk assessment and audit testing and to identify trends, anomalies, and potential control deficiencies. Client Relationship Management: Maintain open, effective, and timely communication with clients during the audit engagement, including timely closure of open questions and requests for additional information, and discussion of matters raised during fieldwork and their potential resolution. Risk Assessment, Emerging Risk and Change: Support audit planning by identifying and assessing changes to credit risk, regulatory developments, technology, business strategies, emerging risks, and significant change initiatives for potential impacts to the control environment. Advisory Engagements: Participate in assigned advisory and risk-focused engagements, providing independent and objective insights into credit risk, governance, risk management, and internal controls. Qualifications: The ideal candidate will have 5+ years’ retail credit experience and 5+ years audit experience. This position requires BMO Credit Qualification for personal loans (commercial loans are desirable but not required). Knowledge: · Undergraduate degree or equivalent with 7 – 10 years of relevant retail and / or business purpose lending or credit risk management experience. · Specific knowledge of all phases of retail and/or business purpose lending covering effective credit administration, policies and procedures and analytical practices, and problem credit identification and management. Comparable knowledge of retail lending practices is desirable. · Solid knowledge of internal controls and risk assessment · Strong knowledge of U.S. Banking Regulations · CPA, CIA, CFA, or CRC designations are desirable. Skills: · Critical thinking skills · Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to work independently and in a team setting · Working level planning and organizing skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities. · Introductory level leadership and managerial skills · Working level relationship management, negotiating, and influencing skills · Good analytical and system thinking skills · Proficient at Microsoft office applications Job posting reflects the Chicago salary range- varies by location Hybrid- 3 days in office weekly required (subject to change) Salary : $75,000.00 - $160,000.00 Pay Type: Salaried The above represents BMO Financial Group’s pay range and type. title: Senior Manager -Internal Audit Business Intelligence & Analytics

The position combines strong technical expertise in business intelligence and data modeling with business acumen, stakeholder management, data governance, and analytical storytelling. The role will lead the design of scalable reporting solutions, executive dashboards, KPI frameworks, thematic and root-cause analysis, and analytics capabilities that help leadership identify emerging risks, understand performance drivers, prioritize remediation, and make informed business decisions. Key Responsibilities Business Intelligence & Analytics Ownership Lead the design, development, and delivery of enterprise BI and analytics solutions supporting Internal Audit Operations, and senior management. Translate complex business requirements into scalable reporting, analytics, and data solutions. Data Quality & Governance Identify source-system data quality issues and assess their impact on downstream analytics and reporting. Develop data-quality reports. Partner with Auditors and technology teams to drive remediation of recurring data issues. Advanced Analytics & AI Identify opportunities to apply AI and advanced analytics to improve analytical efficiency and insight generation. Stakeholder & Team Leadership Lead requirements-gathering sessions and translate business questions into analytical solutions. Manage competing reporting priorities and establish delivery roadmaps. Mentor other team members and promote best practices in analytics, visualization, data modeling, and data storytelling. Serve as a subject matter expert to business and senior leadership. Required Qualifications 8+ years of experience in Business Intelligence Reporting, Data Management, or related disciplines. Significant experience delivering analytics and reporting solutions within complex enterprise environments. Advanced experience with Power BI, SQL Server, DAX, and dimensional data modeling . Strong understanding of data quality, governance, KPI development, and enterprise reporting. Experience supporting Internal Audit Operations, or regulated business functions. Strong experience developing executive dashboards and presenting insights to senior leadership. Ability to translate complex technical and analytical findings into clear business narratives and recommendations. Strong stakeholder management, communication, problem-solving, and leadership skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience in Internal Audit domain. Experience with ServiceNow IRM or similar Governance, Risk, and Compliance platforms. Experience establishing reporting standards, and enterprise analytics operating models. title: Director, Operations Accounting
description: CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at  www.coreweave.com . As the Director, Operations Accounting, you will serve as a strategic leader within CoreWeave’s Accounting Operations organization, with end-to-end ownership of the technical, operational, and reporting activities supporting our global data center operations. You will define and scale the accounting framework that supports rapid infrastructure growth, while ensuring financial integrity, strong internal controls, and alignment with business objectives. You will lead and develop a high-performing global team, partner closely with senior leadership across Operations, FP&A, and Technical Accounting, and play a key role in shaping the financial infrastructure that underpins CoreWeave’s expansion. This role reports to the Head of Operations Accounting and requires a balance of strategic vision, technical expertise, and operational execution — starting hands-on as a player-coach and scaling the team from there.   What You'll Do Own the function end to end: Provide strategic leadership over the technical, operational, and reporting activities supporting CoreWeave’s global data center operations — owning the accounting and month-end close for supply chain and inventory valuation, standard cost and absorption, fixed assets and capital project accounting (CIP), GRIR management, freight and logistics, and procure-to-pay (P2P). Establish the long-term vision: Define and drive a scalable operational accounting framework, including systems, workflows, and organizational design capable of sustaining hyper-growth. Build and operate the control environment: Design and execute a robust, SOX-compliant (or equivalent) control environment across operational and technical accounting processes, driving clean audits and year-over-year reductions in findings. Lead technical & judgment-heavy accounting: Evaluate, document, and implement accounting treatment for complex transactions in partnership with Technical Accounting and Controllership. Support the accounting review and ongoing management of long-term supplier and commercial agreements to ensure appropriate treatment and contractual alignment. Drive systems transformation & integrations: Own the accounting design for supply chain and fixed asset systems and integrations, including ERP implementations, migrations, or upgrades (e.g., NetSuite to Tier-1 platforms like SAP or Oracle), as well as sub-ledger and procurement/WMS integrations. Partner across the business: Act as a trusted advisor to Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, FP&A, IT, Tax, Treasury, and Senior Leadership. Partner closely with FP&A on annual budgets, forecasts, and capital planning strategies to fix data at the source and ensure accurate, timely information flow. Lead audit readiness & operational excellence: Serve as the primary liaison with external auditors and Internal Audit to ensure timely, accurate deliverables. Continuously review existing processes to simplify, automate, shorten close timelines, and reduce operational risk. Build and scale a global team: Start as a hands-on player-coach, then hire, mentor, and grow a high-performing global team from a lean starting point. Who You Are (Required) 10+ years of progressive accounting experience , including senior leadership roles, with broad ownership of technical, operational, cost, or reporting accounting in a high-value, asset-heavy, capital-intensive, or logistics-intensive environment. Strong command of U.S. GAAP and internal controls: Deep technical background in U.S. GAAP as applied to inventory valuation, cost accounting, fixed assets/PP&E, CIP, and procure-to-pay, with proven experience designing and operating SOX-compliant (or equivalent) internal control frameworks. Systems & ERP transformation leadership: Hands-on experience leading or owning the accounting design for an ERP implementation, migration, or major upgrade (NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, Dynamics, or comparable). Proven team builder & player-coach: Demonstrated ability to lead, coach, and scale accounting teams in high-growth, fast-paced environments — equally comfortable setting long-term strategy and diving into technical execution. Exceptional leadership & stakeholder management: Strong executive presence and communication skills, with a track record of partnering cross-functionally with Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, FP&A, and IT to achieve measurable outcomes. We work together each day to foster an inclusive workplace culture where all of our employees feel respected, valued and have an opportunity to contribute to the company’s success. Sets strategy, priorities, and standards for how third-party technology risk is identified, measured, challenged, and reduced across the enterprise. Leads the design, development, and continuous improvement of the third-party technology risk program to meet business, risk appetite, and regulatory expectations. title: Manager, Compliance
description: Recruitment Fraud Alert We’ve learned that scammers are impersonating Commvault team members—including HR and leadership—via email or text. These bad actors may conduct fake interviews and ask for personal information, such as your social security number.   What to know: Commvault does  not  conduct interviews by email or text. We will never ask you to submit sensitive documents (including banking information, SSN, etc) before your first day. Commvault recruiters may contact prospective candidates through LinkedIn and other professional networking platforms regarding career opportunities. If you are unsure whether a recruiting communication is legitimate, review the profile to ensure they have a badge verifying them as a Commvault employee. If you suspect a recruiting scam, please contact us at wwrecruitingteam@commvault.com     About Commvault Commvault (NASDAQ: CVLT) delivers continuous recovery for the AI era. We help organizations stay ready for constant disruption by returning critical data, applications, identities, and AI systems to a clean, trusted state. Our purpose-built recovery solutions span cloud-native and hybrid environments, leveraging AI to enable resilience at enterprise scale. As a Compliance Manager you will serve as a senior member of the GRC team, reporting directly to the Director of GRC and oversee audit and certification maintenance for 12+ commercial audits, as well as planning and readiness for new audits. You will lead audit program operations, partner with teams across the business to strengthen controls and drive remediation, and help expand Commvault’s global compliance program as regulatory, customer, and business needs evolve. This is an opportunity to combine hands-on expertise with strategic planning, turn complex requirements into practical solutions, and make a meaningful impact on the trust organization. What You'll Do... • Lead the ongoing operation and maturity of Commvault’s global audit and certification programs, owning audit maintenance, evidence collection, readiness, and remediation while driving a scalable, top-tier compliance program. • Identify gaps and opportunities to strengthen control maturity, and partner with control owners to implement sustainable improvements. • Oversee the buildout, automation, and ongoing refinement of controls and tests in Commvault’s GRC tool Vanta, partnering with technical teams and control owners to align testing with compliance requirements, validate test results and evidence quality, and establish clear ownership and exception workflows. Drive reliable continuous monitoring and reduce manual effort to support a scalable, mature compliance program. • Define and report actionable compliance metrics covering control effectiveness, monitoring coverage, automation adoption, audit readiness, and remediation progress. Use trends to prioritize improvements and provide clear visibility into program health and maturity. • Partner across Information Security, Legal, Engineering, Product, and other business functions to embed compliance into day-to-day operations, establish clear control accountability, and build practical, sustainable processes that scale with the business. • Work closely with Customer Trust and Risk teams to clarify and communicate audit requirements, escalate gaps and issues to the appropriate stakeholders, and coordinate timely resolution. • Monitor evolving regulations, standards, and industry expectations, assess their impact on Commvault’s compliance programs, and translate relevant changes into prioritized program and control improvements. • Serve as a trusted senior resource for day-to-day compliance guidance, helping stakeholders navigate requirements and make risk-informed decisions while supporting broader priorities across Commvault’s global compliance program. Who You Are... • 7+ years of professional experience in GRC, information security, and/or audit, preferably within a global technology or SaaS organization. • Working knowledge of common security and compliance frameworks and standards, such as ISO 27001, ISO 27701, SOC 2 Type 2, NIST CSF, NIST 800-53, or similar frameworks. title: Independent Tech Risk Manager Sr
description: Position Overview At PNC, our people are our greatest differentiator and competitive advantage in the markets we serve. We are all united in delivering the best experience for our customers. We work together each day to foster an inclusive workplace culture where all of our employees feel respected, valued and have an opportunity to contribute to the company’s success. As an Independent Tech Risk Manager Sr within PNC's BSA/AML organization, you will be based in Pittsburgh, PA; Houston, TX; Dallas, TX; Raleigh, NC; Charlotte, NC; Birmingham, AL; Cleveland, OH; Chicago, IL; Washington DC, Denver, CO; or Phoenix, AZ. The Independent Tech Risk Manager Sr is a highly experienced second line of defense (2LOD) independent contributor responsible for providing credible challenge, oversight, and risk advisory services across the enterprise fraud risk management program. This role serves as a senior subject matter expert on fraud risk, partnering with business, operations, technology, and risk leaders to identify emerging fraud threats, assess fraud control effectiveness, evaluate risk management practices, and ensure alignment with regulatory expectations and enterprise risk management standards. The position operates with a high degree of autonomy and influence, driving risk-informed decision making and escalating material fraud risks through appropriate governance channels while maintaining strong 2LOD independence. The role is expected to bring deep industry expertise, strategic insight, and thought leadership to strengthen the organization's fraud risk posture. Required Qualifications • Minimum 15 years of experience in fraud risk management, financial crimes, fraud operations, fraud strategy, fraud analytics, fraud investigations, or related disciplines within banking, payments, financial services, fintech, or other regulated financial institutions. • Demonstrated expertise across multiple fraud domains, including payment fraud, account takeover, identity fraud, digital fraud, check fraud, card fraud, and emerging fraud threats. • Strong understanding of enterprise risk management, operational risk management, and second line of defense responsibilities. • Proven ability to provide effective challenge and influence senior leaders without direct reporting authority. • Experience interacting with regulators, auditors, risk committees, and executive leadership. • Strong analytical, communication, presentation, and executive briefing skills. • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Risk Management, Criminal Justice, Information Security, or a related field. title: Financial Operations Manager
description: BitGo (NYSE: BTGO) is the digital asset infrastructure company delivering custody, wallets, staking, trading, financing, stablecoins, and settlement services from regulated cold storage. Since 2013, BitGo has focused on accelerating the transition of the financial system to a digital asset economy. BitGo maintains a global presence and multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, the first federally chartered digital asset trust bank owned by a publicly traded company. Today, BitGo serves thousands of institutions, including many of the industry's top brands, financial institutions, exchanges, and platforms, and millions of investors worldwide. For more information, visit www.bitgo.com . This role will require being full-time onsite at our Palo Alto office to support collaborative team dynamics and innovative problem-solving. About the Role: We are seeking a hands-on Financial Operations Manager to support and strengthen our finance operations within a fast-paced, regulated environment. This role blends financial control, treasury oversight, regulatory coordination, and cross-functional business partnership. You will help ensure operational excellence across financial reporting, liquidity management, and internal controls, while delivering actionable insights to support leadership decision-making. This role is well-suited to a proactive operator who thrives in high-growth environments, takes ownership, and continuously improves processes. What You’ll Do: Financial Operations & Reporting: Support the day-to-day finance function, ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting. Contribute to monthly, quarterly, and year-end close processes. Support external audits and financial reviews, ensuring timely and accurate deliverables. Maintain accurate books and records, including reconciliations and supporting documentation. Strengthen internal controls, documentation standards, and compliance processes. Partner with business leaders to align financial insights with operational objectives. Treasury & Liquidity Management: Oversee cash flow monitoring and liquidity management. Partner with treasury on forecasting and funding strategies. Support treasury-related initiatives to enhance capital planning and efficiency. title: Head of Finance
description: About Highnote  Founded in 2020 by a team of leaders from Braintree, PayPal, and Lending Club, Highnote is the unified platform for embedded finance, built for modern issuing, acquiring, credit, ledger, and real-time money movement. With an integrated ledger, full program management, and a purpose-built architecture, we help companies design financial products around their customers and launch faster with greater control.  We’ve raised $145M+ and have grown our team to 140+ employees across 25+ US States, with headquarters in San Francisco. Along the way, we’ve built one of the most experienced payments teams in the industry. We’re fast-moving and hands-on, and we believe everyone deserves a seat at the table. Our values of customer obsession, executional excellence, intentional inclusion, guide how we build the payment products of tomorrow's business needs. We’re looking for people who want to help shape the future of payments. Job Description  This is a leadership role for a finance leader who wants to shape the direction of a high-growth payments company. Reporting to the COO and partnering closely with the CEO and the rest of the leadership team, you will be the person who looks ahead, reads what the numbers are telling us, and proactively lays out the financial moves the company should make. You will not wait to be asked for analysis. You will bring it, defend it, and help us act on it. Payments is a business of fine margins and constant tradeoffs, where economics, mix, and cost all move together. We are looking for a leader who understands those dynamics, sees around corners, forms a clear point of view, and turns it into recommendations the leadership team can act on with confidence. You will also stand behind those numbers when it counts, including with our auditors, where your judgment and the integrity of our reporting matter. We want someone who is genuinely forward-leaning on technology and AI, and who will use it to transform how our financial operations run. The goal is to take our analysis to the next level, using automation and AI to produce sharper, faster, and deeper insight and to give the team more room for the thinking that moves the business, all while preserving the auditability and control our reporting depends on. What you will own Financial and analytical leadership. Proactively analyze the business, spot where we are heading financially, and recommend the steps we should be taking, ahead of being asked. Own the strategic financial narrative: what is driving performance, what it means for the plan, and where the risks and opportunities are. Run scenario and sensitivity work so leadership can see the financial impact of major decisions, new products, and customer changes before they are made. Be a genuine partner to the CEO and COO, translating financial reality into clear, defensible guidance that shapes company decisions. Planning and reporting. Guide the annual operating plan and regular forecasting, working with the team that runs the day-to-day modeling, and hold the overall view of revenue, gross profit, operating expense, and burn. Deliver a clean, insightful reporting package to the leadership team and the board that explains what happened, why, and what we should do about it. Capital, burn, and treasury. Manage burn and runway with a clear point of view on where spend earns its keep and where it does not. Own cash flow, treasury, and banking relationships, and support debt facilities and covenant compliance. Support equity and debt fundraising with the model, the diligence materials, and the analysis investors will expect. Controls and audit. Partner with the Controller, who owns the monthly close and tax, to keep reporting accurate, timely, and audit-ready, and to strengthen internal controls as we scale. Stand behind the company's financial positions and judgments with our external auditors, and defend the decisions we make when they are examined. Keep financial reporting compliant with GAAP and appropriate for our size and phase. Strategic initiatives. Lead the financial workstreams behind our strategic and regulatory initiatives, including the financial planning, projections, and capital considerations they require. Transforming financial operations. Own the finance technology stack, from the NetSuite core to the tools around it, and set the standard for how a high-performing finance function runs. Use automation and AI to transform financial operations across forecasting, reporting, invoicing, and reconciliation, taking analysis to the next level and freeing the team for higher-value work, while preserving auditability and control at every step. Team and leadership. Lead, coach, and raise the bar for a strong existing finance team, and build the organization the company needs as it scales.
